# Third pass — 2026-08-30 21:50 BST. **Not a green light.**

The headline number is wrong, and I broke the `free_network` guard on the first attempt.

---

## 1. The board is red, and it was red before today's nine items

**Claimed:** 4521 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
**Measured** (`python3 -m pytest bench/tests -q`, 327 s, twice):

```
2 failed, 4515 passed, 4 skipped, 18 warnings in 327.28s
```

The 4 skips are `test_br2_keys_are_split_out_2026-08-27.py` — key store outside the repo, honest environment skips. The two failures are not equal:

**(a) `test_experiment_run_ledger…::test_the_committed_ledger_matches_bench_logs` — sandbox artefact, will not reproduce for you.** The drift is one paragraph: *"12 aborted invocations wrote an empty directory."* Git cannot carry empty directories, so a fresh copy regenerates a ledger without them. Discount it.

**(b) `test_falsifier_cannot_read_the_key.py::test_the_guard_rejects_nothing_else_in_the_whole_tracked_archive` — real, on tracked files, and pre-existing.** The exploit guard rejects **17 archived falsifiers where the test expects 2**, across exp42/44/46/47/48/49. Every offending `*_report.json` is `git ls-files`-tracked, so this is not the carried-ignored-files change.

I checked out `08e3e0d` (the commit before the nine items) into a clean worktree with tracked files only. **It fails there too.** So the 4521/0/0 board was never measured on a clean tree at any of today's commits.

Rate, cross-verified with two independent Wilson implementations (statsmodels `proportion_confint`, and scipy `norm.ppf` by hand — agree to 1e-12):

| | value |
|---|---|
| archived falsifier sources | 469 |
| rejected by `scan_falsifier_source` | 17 |
| false-positive rate | 3.62%, 95% Wilson **[2.28%, 5.73%]** |
| rate the test pins | 2/469 = 0.43% |

The interval excludes the expected rate. The test's own docstring states the decision rule: *"If a future rule change makes this fail, the rule is blocking honest work."* `bench/falsifier_verify.py` last changed at `f9d4f5b`; the corpus grew at `043a0a8`. Nobody re-ran the guard against the enlarged corpus. **Fifteen honest falsifiers are being blocked and the project has been reporting green over the top of it.**

---

## 2. `free_network` — I reached a metered endpoint from inside the window. Twice.

This is the most serious finding available today, and the brief predicted the right place to look.

I wrote three adversarial tests marked `@pytest.mark.free_network` and ran them. Verbatim output:

```
POPEN_ALLOWED out="CHILD_CONNECTED ('162.159.140.245', 443)"     # api.openai.com:443
IP_CONNECT_ALLOWED to 172.66.0.243                                # api.openai.com:443
NAMED_DENIED ConnectionError('CDSFL netguard denied tcp -> api.openai.com...')
```

Only the third — the case the 8 new tests cover — is denied.

**Hole 1: the subprocess door opens wide inside the window.** `conftest.py:310`:

```python
if _free_window and exe not in _PAID_BINARIES:
    return _orig["popen_init"](self, args, *a, **kw)
```

That early return skips the `"https://" in joined` check *and* the entire `_NETWORK_BINARIES` set. `_PAID_BINARIES` has four entries. Measured delta, same command inside and outside:

```
INSIDE_WINDOW:  curl https://api.openai.com/v1/models  -> ALLOWED rc=0
OUTSIDE_WINDOW: curl https://api.openai.com/v1/models  -> DENIED  netguard denied subprocess -> curl
```

And a child process makes its own sockets, which the in-process `_PAID_HOSTS` list cannot see at all. `curl`, `wget`, `httpie`, `gh`, `pip`, `npm` all became reachable, along with any URL-bearing argv.

**Hole 2: the deny-list is name-based, so an IP literal walks through.** `_free_allowed` compares a string against hostnames; `172.66.0.243` equals no entry and ends with no entry, so it returns `True`. Any code that resolves separately then connects by address — a proxy CONNECT, an SDK with a pinned IP — is unguarded.

**Why the 8 new tests missed both.** Every one of them calls `G._free_allowed(host)` — the pure name predicate — and never exercises `_guard_popen_init` or `_guard_connect` with the window open. The tests assert the *policy*; the holes are in the *enforcement*. `test_free_network_does_not_weaken_the_money_guard_2026-08-30.py` is honest about what it checks and is still not evidence for the claim it is titled with.

**Fix**: inside the window, `_guard_popen_init` must fall through to the existing `_NETWORK_BINARIES`/URL check rather than returning early — subtract `claude` from the denial, don't skip the check. And `_free_allowed` should reject any host that parses as an IP unless it is in `_free_ips`.

---

## 3. The fenced-falsifier repair is a net regression on the routing ladder

Old (`08e3e0d:4437`): `r"```[^\n]*\n(.*?)```"`
New (`1f43179:4517`): `r"```[^\n]*\n(.*?)\n[ \t]*```[ \t]*(?=\r?\n|$)"`

Differential over both patterns through the full `ast.parse` + runnability filter, then re-confirmed against the imported `_extract_routing_falsifier` itself:

| model reply shape | old | new | |
|---|---|---|---|
| ` ``` ` then ` — run that.` on the same line | kept | **lost** | regression |
| closing fence glued to the last code line | kept | **lost** | regression |
| ` ``` ` followed by `.` | kept | **lost** | regression |
| **two blocks, first closer has trailing prose** | kept 2nd | **lost both** | **cascade** |
| normal block, CRLF, indented closer | same | same | ok |

The fourth row is the one that matters. With a malformed first closer, `(.*?)` scans past it, past the *second block's opening fence*, and pairs with the second block's closer. `findall` then resumes beyond that point. One trailing word after a closing fence destroys **every block in the reply**, including well-formed ones. Verified on the real function: `_extract_routing_falsifier(F)` → `''`.

This feeds the routing ladder, whose failure mode is a silent `"ladder exhausted"` — the exact defect the docstring at `:4475` says it was written to close. The old pattern was too permissive; the new one is brittle in a way that fails *closed and silently*. Neither pattern handles a four-backtick fence, which is standard markdown for a block containing backticks.

**Fix**: keep the alone-on-its-line requirement, but anchor the search per-block with `re.finditer` from each opening fence, and fall back to the permissive closer when the strict one finds none before the next opening fence.

I could not measure how often models emit a trailing-text closer — the 31 files in `logs/` are JSON-escaped and gave 4 blocks, too few to state a rate. I am not claiming a frequency.

---

## 4. `discrimination_control_ask`: the chain closes, but the runner will tell you it didn't

The ask→parse→store→consume path **is** complete — I traced it and it holds. `_ASK_CORRECTED_COPY` at `:6900` → `_gate_falsifier_directive` → `_runnable_falsifier_s2`; response text → `_ingest_corrected_copies` (`:10629`) → `_accept_corrected_copy` writes `entry["corrected_copy"]` (`:3533`) → `run_discrimination_control` (`:3857`) reads exactly `falsifier_code` ∧ `corrected_copy`. The parse side was built on 12 Aug and is generic; today's change turned on the supply. The sim does not bypass it — the shim patches `dispatch_to_model`, not `_dispatch_single_model`.

Three defects sit on top of it:

**(a) The runner prints a false statement, 23 lines before contradicting itself.** `reference_runner_v2.py:9633-9638` still executes:

```
** discrimination_control_ask=True IS NOT WIRED — it is read by no code in this runner. **
   ...Setting it arms nothing.
```

then at `:9657` arms it. The header comment at `:9626` still says *"confirmed by AST: 1 write, 0 reads."* The sim run sets the flag `True`, so **this will print on the next run**, and you will read the runner asserting the repair was not applied. Delete both `_log` calls and the stale comment.

**(b) The ask is nested inside `if enable_tools:` (`:6895`) — i.e. `falsifier_gate_enabled`.** With the ask on and the gate off, no ask is emitted and nothing says so. That is the same placebo shape the wire was written to remove. Masked in the sim only because `run_simulated_experiment.py:132` happens to set the gate on.

**(c) No test pins the wire.** `_ASK_CORRECTED_COPY` appears in zero test files. `test_discrimination_control.py:474` asserts the default is `False`. Line `:9657` could be deleted and the suite stays green — which is precisely how this flag survived from 21 Aug to today.

**On "0 of 58 with both inputs"**: that figure appears as prose in three places and is computed by no committed code. The breakdown in `Six_Repairs_And_A_Panel_2026-08-30.md:69` is the substance: exp45 had 23 falsifiers and 0 copies; the sim had 0 falsifiers and 19 copies. The intersection is empty for **two independent reasons** and the ask addresses one. Expect the control to fire this time only if the sim also produces falsifiers on the same entries.

|---|---|

| Fable `MODEL_SPECS` + `Fable.toml` | **true** — `runner_core.py:106` with `_provenance: "inherited from CC2 2026-08-30; not measured"`; `bench/cdsfl_registry/models/Fable.toml` |

**On the tripwire** (`run_simulated_experiment.py:212`): it patches `socket.getaddrinfo` only, and its `_PAID` tuple has 5 hosts where `conftest._PAID_HOSTS` has 8 — it omits `api.groq.com`, `api.mistral.ai`, `api.cohere.ai`. `bench/run_benchmark.py:650` dispatches to `api.groq.com` and `:686` to `models.inference.ai.azure.com`, which **neither** list contains. Two hand-maintained copies of the same money-critical constant, already divergent. Same IP-literal and proxy blind spots as §2. It is a useful backstop, not a guarantee.

## 6. What will still be silent on the next simulated run

Enumerated by AST over `RunnerConfig` defaults overlaid with the sim's kwargs, not by intuition. Twelve flags on; **fifteen paths dark**:

`apply_fixes_back_enabled`, `apply_fixes_back_seed`, `burst_mode='off'` *(sim override)*, `discrimination_control_blocks`, `hardened_gate_enabled`, `hierarchical_novelty_convergence`, `hil_review`, `immune_memory_enabled`, `immune_memory_consume_rk0`, `latent_tagger_enabled`, `panel_cwd`, `resume`, `severity_calibration_enabled`, `stall_gamma_termination_enabled`, `target_kind`.

Plus, stated explicitly in the harness: `_ouroboros` shadow cell is not enabled, so the cell whose tests you just un-skipped is dark in the run itself.

Three specific silences I'd flag:

- **`discrimination_control_blocks=False`.** The ask is on; blocking is off. The control will *record* a discrimination outcome and change no verdict. That is your standing ruling and correct — but the run will not demonstrate the control affecting anything.
- **`stall_gamma_terminate=1.01` / `stall_gamma_advisory=1.01`.** Above 1.0, so stall detection cannot fire at any gamma. Intentional; note it before reading "no stall" as a result.
- **The routing ladder's own silence**, from §3. A trailing-text closer produces `"ladder exhausted"` with `rungs_reached` non-empty — the new telemetry will show a rung *was* reached and returned nothing, which is exactly right and will point at the regex if you read it.

**One prediction I formed and then killed.** I expected `gamma_telemetry_only_until=20` over ~7 rounds to render gamma inert. It does not. That flag governs `_check_gamma_gate` on `gamma_all` — telemetry in the live config too (14 ≥ 12). The active side, `_check_gamma_alt_convergence`, takes `gamma_critical` as a parameter and never consults it (`:5319`). Gamma is live. Recording the falsification because a wrong version of this claim would have argued for demoting gamma, which is the failure mode you named.

---

## 7. What we all missed again — twice over

**The `free_network` change silently made the suite network-dependent.** I simulated an outage by closing the window while keeping the marker:

```
FAILED test_ouroboros_realwork.py::test_real_paper_fetched_read_and_briefed
FAILED test_ouroboros_realwork.py::test_shadow_log_captures_briefs
2 failed, 18 passed
```

Two of the three newly-enabled tests **hard-fail without network**, and they now run **by default**. `conftest.py`'s founding property — *"it simulates a machine with no network... and the suite stays green"* — is gone. On a plane, in an egress-less CI, or during an arXiv outage, `pytest bench/tests` goes red and will read as a code defect. The deny-list shape makes this worse, not better: retrieval follows a DOI to any publisher, so the suite's runtime and colour now depend on hosts nobody enumerated. The `network` marker existed for exactly this and was bypassed rather than used.

**And the second miss, which is the pattern:** three consecutive reviews have now each found a claimed repair that was not real, and this time it is the headline. `4521 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped` was reported without being run on the tree it describes. The falsifier-guard red predates today by several commits, on tracked files, reproducible in a clean worktree in 0.8 seconds. Nobody looked, because the number was already believed.

That is the thing to fix before the run: not the guard, not the regex — **the habit of reporting a suite result that was not produced by the suite.** By your own founding principle, a green board is a claim like any other, and it was confirmed by agreement rather than by execution.

## Recommendation

**Hold the run.** Four blockers, in order:

1. Re-run the suite and publish the real number, or fix the guard's 15 false positives.
2. Close both `free_network` holes; move the enforcement tests off `_free_allowed` onto `_guard_popen_init`/`_guard_connect`.
3. Fix the regex cascade — a routing ladder that loses blocks silently is the failure this project exists to catch.
4. Delete the false `IS NOT WIRED` log before it appears in your run output.

Items 1 and 4 are minutes. 2 and 3 are the substantive work.
